changed_scope: Romance / Can Casual Sex or a Situationship Actually Be Honest?

preservation_units.meaning: A casual-sex agreement does not prevent bodily attachment; post-sex attachment can arise despite stated intentions.
A person may candidly want sex while honestly not knowing whether they want a serious relationship.
Candor about present intentions does not settle obligations if sex creates pregnancy; contraception is imperfect and concrete responsibility questions remain.
Partners can test/disclose STI knowledge and must explicitly admit when they do not know.
preservation_units.candidate_mapping: You can test for STIs and tell each other what you know. If you don't know, say so.

preservation_units.meaning: Mutual sincere agreement that sex is casual does not control later attachment.
preservation_units.required_context: contrasted with comparatively tractable STI disclosure
preservation_units.candidate_mapping: Attachment is less cooperative. Both of you can mean it when you say this is only sex, and then one of you wakes up attached anyway.

preservation_units.meaning: Joel leaves open the possibility that people who are very numb/robotic about sex may not attach.
preservation_units.candidate_mapping: final sentence of changed paragraph unchanged

preservation_units.source_ref: loving poly community / mutual use paragraph
preservation_units.meaning: Outside a loving poly community or tribe Joel considers honest casual sex nearly impossible because partners must care what happens afterward; reciprocal use does not redeem using another for pleasure.
Claims of wanting only fun can conceal a hope for love that may be recognized only when it fails.
Situationships are often sex-based, under-defined relationships; refusing the label does not erase responsibility or superficiality.
preservation_units.required_context: situationship subsection within same natural section
preservation_units.candidate_mapping: situationship definition and responsibility paragraphs unchanged

preservation_units.source_ref: why are you making this heavy exchange
preservation_units.meaning: The section acknowledges the genuine appeal/cost question behind resistance to making casual arrangements serious, then answers by asking whether the arrangement fulfills or drains.
Joel's relationship with H. was deep and non-superficial but romantically uneven, so it only partly resembles a situationship.
Labels do not create commitment but can reveal whether partners understand the relationship similarly; lived relational depth creates practical commitment.
The person apparently winning a casual arrangement can still be miserable and empty.
Taking pregnancy, attachment, and post-sex obligations seriously would make casual sex much rarer; Joel judges many defenses of it as self-dishonest.
A less damaging form of casual lovemaking would require a community where people and bonds are not disposable and children have a village.
